papers.title_en: Rethinking Post-Training Quantization for Large Vision-Language Models
papers.authors: Minchan Kang, Kyeonghye Park, Seoyoung Cho, Junhee Lee, Daeshik Kim, Yucheol Cho
papers.evidence: 面向大型视觉-语言模型的权重-激活后训练量化分析
papers.tldr: 大视觉语言模型PTQ在低比特权重-激活量化下性能明显下降，已有校准策略难解。作者发现离群值主导逐通道权重与逐token激活的共享范围，导致多数值分辨率不足甚至被映射为零。为此提出RRQ，以局部Hadamard变换、分组量化和高效分组执行改进量化表示。在8个多模态任务上，W4A4下8B模型保留超96%全精度性能、32B超99%，并降低推理时间与内存。
papers.abstract_en: Post-training quantization (PTQ) compresses large vision-language models (LVLMs) by calibrating quantization parameters on a small dataset without retraining. However, despite increasingly sophisticated calibration strategies, prior methods suffer substantial performance degradation under low-bit weight--activation quantization. To understand this degradation, we locate where quantization error is concentrated and examine the corresponding weight and activation distributions. We observe that a few outliers dominate the ranges shared by per-channel (PC) weights and per-token (PT) activations, leaving insufficient resolution for most values and mapping many of them to zero. These findings motivate a shift in focus from calibration refinement to the underlying quantization representation. We therefore present Rotate-and-Refine Quantization (RRQ) as a simple, effective baseline for LVLM PTQ, combining local Hadamard transforms with group quantization and efficient group-aware execution. Across 8 multimodal tasks and diverse quantization settings, RRQ substantially outperforms baselines while reducing inference time and memory usage. At W4A4, it retains over 96\% of full-precision performance on 8B models and over 99\% on a 32B model, compared with less than 8\% for these baselines. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/kmc3661/RRQ

papers.title_en: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
papers.authors: Natalia Frumkin, Alireza Khodamoradi, Kristof Denolf, Eric Dellinger, Stuart Biles
papers.evidence: 面向LLM推理的微缩放格式后训练量化配方
papers.tldr: 低精度LLM推理中，MXFP4/NVFP4等微缩放格式的精度取决于数值格式与旋转、PTQ及scale选择的交互。作者跨六个LLM系统比较MXFP6、MXFP4、NVFP4，发现有效配方格式相关，并提出免校准Midmax缓解2的幂块scale截断误差。MXFP4显著受益于旋转和纠错PTQ，MXFP6激活配MXFP4权重可恢复大部分4bit损失，并在Llama-3.1-8B匹配或超过BF16基线。结果强调需按格式组合量化技术，而非直接迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in low-precision representation have introduced several microscaling numerical formats for LLM quantization. By sharing a scale factor across groups of 16 or 32 elements, these formats enable aggressive low-precision quantization with minimal accuracy degradation, particularly when combined with modern PTQ algorithms. Their accuracy depends on how the numerical format interacts with rotation, PTQ, and scale selection. We study the composability of PTQ configurations across six LLMs and three microscaling formats: MXFP6, MXFP4, and NVFP4, systematically varying Hadamard rotation granularity, PTQ algorithm, and scale-selection strategy. Our central finding is that effective quantization recipes are format dependent: both MXFP4 and NVFP4 support accurate 4-bit inference, but techniques that benefit one do not necessarily transfer to the other. MXFP4 benefits substantially from rotation and error-correcting PTQ, whereas NVFP4 gains less from rotation, consistent with its finer-grained scales capturing more within-block variation. Building on these findings, we introduce Midmax, a calibration-free scale-selection strategy that mitigates clipping error in power-of-two block scales and improves accuracy across a majority of the evaluated MXFP4 configurations. We show that pairing MXFP6 activations with MXFP4 weights recovers most of the accuracy lost at 4-bit and, on Llama-3.1-8B, matches or exceeds our in-house BF16 baseline. An additional study finds that augmenting MXFP4 with a per-tensor macroscale, a mechanism intrinsic to NVFP4, does not improve average accuracy, suggesting that global rescaling alone does not address the limitations of E8M0 block scales for MXFP4 quantization. Together, these results provide practical guidance for combining numerical formats, rotation, PTQ, and scale selection for accurate low-precision LLM inference.

papers.title_en: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
papers.authors: Yufeng Huang
papers.evidence: 面向大语言模型的整数组量化方法及 INT4 内核
papers.tldr: 分组量化可提升低比特大模型精度，但权重分组会阻碍标准整数MMA覆盖完整点积，影响GPU推理效率。作者提出Shifter Quantization，通过拼接并移位共享比特重构原生位宽整数操作数，并衍生适配INT4内核的SHI变体。在2/4/8比特设置下，其投影误差、KL散度和预填充/解码吞吐均优于分组量化、NInfer与vLLM FP8等基线。该工作为低比特LLM提供兼顾精度与原生整数计算效率的紧凑量化表示。
papers.abstract_en: Groupwise quantization is used in LLM quantization to improve accuracy at low bit widths, but grouping weights keeps standard integer MMA from spanning the full dot product for efficient GPU inference. We develop a new quantization method, Shifter Quantization (SQ), that reconstructs native-width integer operands by appending and shifting shared bits. To further extend the efficiency, we develop a special variant of SQ, Shifter Integer (SHI), to use INT4 kernels. We show that SQ and SHI formats perform better than standard groupwise quantization in quality, as measured by projection error and KL divergence, and in inference speed, as measured during decoding and prefill. For low precision like 2-bit quantization, SQ2 and SHI2 achieve 2.71-3.77x the 4,096-token prefill throughput of llama.cpp on a Q2_K checkpoint and reduce WikiText-2 KL by 6.6-7.8%. For mid precision like 4-bit quantization, SQ4 achieves 1.43-2.47x the prefill throughput of NInfer's groupwise-integer baselines across the tested models and prompt lengths, with 24-40% lower KL than the NInfer baselines. For high precision like 8-bit quantization, SQ8 achieves 27.4% higher batch-one prefill throughput and 72.7% lower KL than vLLM's online FP8.

papers.title_en: Hi3R-VLA: Grounding Semantics and Actions in 3D
papers.authors: Shizhe Chen, Paul Pacaud, Cordelia Schmid
papers.evidence: 将视觉、语言与动作锚定在显式三维几何中的机器人操作VLA策略
papers.tldr: 现有VLA模型虽引入3D几何，但如何有效用于精准且可泛化的动作预测仍是核心难题。Hi3R-VLA将空间对齐的视觉语言特征融入点云，并把动作锚定在同一3D坐标系，用3D-RoPE增强动作到点的注意。不足250M可训练参数下，在多个仿真基准与真机任务达SOTA。工作验证了3D内语义融合及观测—动作空间对齐的重要性。
papers.abstract_en: While recent vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly incorporate 3D geometry, how to effectively exploit it for precise and generalizable action prediction remains a central challenge. We introduce Hi3R-VLA, a 3D policy that grounds heterogeneous modalities - vision, language, and action - in explicit 3D geometry for robotic manipulation. Our model integrates spatially-aligned visual features and language conditioning into point cloud representations, enriching scene geometry with fine-grained, task-relevant semantics. It then anchors low-level control commands in the same 3D coordinate frame and uses 3D-RoPE enhanced action-to-point attention over coarse-to-fine point features to model geometric relationships between action targets and observed points. Our analysis demonstrates the importance of semantic fusion within 3D and spatial alignment between observations and actions. With fewer than 250M trainable parameters, Hi3R-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance on RoboCasa, RLBench, RoboTwin2, DexJoCo and DexSuite across diverse manipulation tasks and embodiments, from single-arm and dual-arm grippers to dexterous hands. Real-robot evaluations further demonstrate its effectiveness in the physical world. The model, code and dataset are publicly released at https://cshizhe.github.io/projects/hi3r_vla.html.

papers.title_en: KeyMemVLA: Subtask-Guided Key Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Yongwei Zhang, Tao Chen, Sicheng Ma, Yuanzhe Xing, Pengwei Zhang, Yongen Zhao, Yaoqing Hu, Zhikun She, Ce Hao
papers.evidence: 面向长程操作、带子任务引导关键记忆的视觉-语言-动作策略
papers.tldr: 长时程机器人操作需在有限记忆预算下保留能消解阶段歧义的历史。KeyMemVLA 用子任务引导关键记忆：两级标注选取满足进度指示或决策证据保留的子任务，将其末帧作为关键帧监督在线记忆写入，并由共享视觉-语言骨干联合学习子任务、动作与关键帧预测。推理时先推断当前子任务，再据此预测动作和未来记忆写入位置；在 RMBench-M(n)、RoboTwin-MeM、KMBench 及真实任务上平均成功率优于基线。该工作表明稀疏关键记忆与在线进度推断结合，可提升历史依赖控制。
papers.abstract_en: Memory-dependent long-horizon manipulation requires vision-language-action (VLA) policies to infer task progress and recall evidence absent from current observations. Under a limited memory budget, the challenge is to retain history that resolves stage ambiguity and supports subsequent decisions. We present KeyMemVLA, a subtask-guided key memory framework based on progress indication and decision-evidence retention. A two-level annotation process selects subtasks satisfying either criterion and labels their final frames as keyframes to supervise online memory writes. A shared vision-language backbone jointly learns subtask, action, and keyframe prediction. At inference, the policy first predicts the current subtask from the instruction, visual context, and memory, then uses this semantic condition to predict actions and future memory-write positions. Actual observations are retained at the selected times during execution. We introduce KMBench to evaluate active memory retention for decisions across subtasks. Evaluations on RMBench-$M(n)$, RoboTwin-MeM, KMBench, and real-world manipulation tasks show higher average success rates than the compared baselines. Ablation studies and representation analysis support the roles of key memory and explicit task-progress semantics. These results highlight the value of coupling sparse key memory with online progress inference for history-dependent control.

papers.title_en: GeoVLDrive: Geometry-Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: JiaHui Huang, Songyan Zhang, Hanbing Li, Hanchao Leng, Kuiyuan Yang, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Chen Lv
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶的几何锚定视觉-语言-动作规划器
papers.tldr: 现有视觉-语言-动作规划器虽继承了预训练模型的语义知识，但其推理很少真正扎根于三维场景结构及其随时间演化。GeoVLDrive 通过门控交叉注意力将 3D 基础模型的多层特征注入视觉语言主干，并用结构化隐式思维链分别监督未来几何、关键智能体运动与元动作，再由动作专家生成并排序轨迹。在 NAVSIM v1 与 v2 上分别取得 91.8 PDMS 和 90.9 EPDMS。作者同时提出 NAVSIM 3DQA 基准，推动可度量的三维空间与运动理解评测。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) planners inherit semantic knowledge from pretrained vision-language models, but their reasoning is rarely grounded in 3D scene structure and its evolution over time. We introduce GeoVLDrive, a geometry-grounded VLA framework for 3D spatiotemporal reasoning and planning. Multi-layer features from a 3D foundation model augment the vision-language backbone through gated cross-attention. A structured latent chain of thought (CoT) organizes future scene geometry, key-agent motion, and meta-actions into ordered, separately supervised latent states. An action expert generates trajectory proposals from these states and multi-layer scene features, and ranks them using scene-grounded, interacting score tokens. We also introduce NAVSIM 3DQA to train and evaluate metric 3D spatial and motion understanding. GeoVLDrive achieves 91.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2. On NAVSIM 3DQA, the geometry-grounded backbone scores 89.2% overall, 4.6 percentage points above the fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-2B baseline. On LingoQA, the backbone achieves 68.6% Lingo-Judge accuracy.

papers.title_en: MXI-MemICL: Towards In-Context Robot Manipulation through Self-Retrieved Interaction Memory
papers.authors: Jialong Peng, Shihao Zhou, Feng Yan, Wen Xiao, Haozheng Wang, Wenqi Ren, Wenyuan Sheng, Jian Qiao, Jiaxu Miao, Lin Ma, Chao Yang
papers.evidence: 面向视觉-语言-动作机器人操作的记忆引导上下文学习
papers.tldr: 机器人上下文学习常受限于稀缺昂贵的交互数据或额外标注，且跨任务泛化不足。MXI-MemICL将演示视为可检索记忆，用视觉-动作因果编码器把动作与效果转为可复用经验，并由意图预测器检索下一阶段经验。检索经验经经验令牌前缀和门控交叉注意力注入VLA语言主干，引导动作生成。在RoboCasa365与RoboTwin 2.0上成功率较基线提升8.2%和14.4%，真机提升9.0%，展示无需大规模预训练或专用标注的记忆引导ICL潜力。
papers.abstract_en: In-context learning (ICL) offers robots a way to acquire new skills from a single demonstration without parameter updates. However, existing robotic ICL methods either rely on large-scale pretraining constrained by scarce, costly robot interaction data or require additional annotations yet struggle to generalize across tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose MXI-MemICL, a framework for memory-guided ICL in vision-language-action (VLA) models. By treating demonstrations as retrievable memory, MXI-MemICL enables in-context manipulation without additional large-scale pretraining or specialized annotations. Specifically, a visual-action causal encoder turns actions and their observed effects in demonstrations and completed interactions into reusable memory to guide execution. To retrieve experience suited to upcoming execution, an intention predictor forecasts the next stage's intent and uses it to query memory. The retrieved experience conditions the language backbone through experience-token prefixes and gated cross-attention, guiding action generation with a learned gate that regulates its influence. MXI-MemICL improves success over the baseline by +8.2% and +14.4% on RoboCasa365 and RoboTwin 2.0. Real-robot experiments show a +9.0% gain, with demonstrations adding +5.0% on seen and +16.7% on unseen tasks. The code will be made publicly available.

papers.title_en: HiCal: Offline Calibration for Hierarchical Scale Encoding in Accurate HiF4 Quantization
papers.authors: Zhiyuan Zhang, Yanzhao Li, Hui Dong, Sifan Cheng, Mingen Zheng, Hui Wang
papers.evidence: 离线校准优化分层块尺度以提升低比特大模型量化精度
papers.tldr: 针对HiF4分块浮点量化中分层尺度编码依赖传统舍入与固定扩展阈值、难以匹配张量统计特征的问题，HiCal提出离线校准方法，联合优化全局E6M2尺度舍入偏置及两级二进制尺度扩展阈值。校准参数离线确定并在推理时固定，仍保留按块局部值自适应的确定性编码，无需逐块多候选搜索。在合成与真实激活分布上，量化MSE较原HiF4降低9.91%至23.50%，Qwen3-8B真实激活降低13.00%；六个基准端到端平均分分别提升0.91和1.25个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: Block floating-point (BFP) quantization is widely adopted for efficient low-bit large language model (LLM) inference, where the choice of block scales plays a critical role in quantization accuracy. HiFloat4 (HiF4) employs a hierarchical scale encoding scheme consisting of a global E6M2 scale and two levels of binary scale extensions. However, its conventional rounding rule and fixed scale extension thresholds may not fully capture the statistical characteristics of the quantized tensors in practice, leading to suboptimal scale representations. In this work, we propose HiCal, an offline calibration approach that improves HiF4 quantization accuracy by refining the encoding decisions across all three scale levels. Specifically, we introduce a calibrated rounding bias for the Level-1 E6M2 scale and optimize the scale-extension thresholds at Levels 2 and 3 based on the empirical distributions of local group magnitudes. The resulting calibration parameters are determined offline and remain fixed during inference, while the hierarchical encoding continues to adapt to individual blocks through their local values. This design eliminates the need for per-block multi-candidate scale search while preserving the original deterministic HiF4 encoding procedure. Experiments across five synthetic and real activation distributions show that the proposed method reduces quantization MSE by 9.91%-23.50% relative to the original HiF4 scheme, including a 13.00% reduction on real Qwen3-8B activations. End-to-end evaluations across six benchmarks further show average-score improvements of 0.91 and 1.25 percentage points on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, respectively, without per-block multi-candidate search during inference.

papers.title_en: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Haoyuan Li, Wei Huang, Jiehong Lin, Shengrong Zhang, Chenzhi Liu, Shengchao Zhou, Hehe Fan, Xiaojuan Qi, Yi Yang
papers.evidence: 面向长程机器人操作VLA策略的进度引导强化学习
papers.tldr: 长程机器人操作中，稀疏的成功或失败反馈难以定位策略瓶颈，重复执行完整任务 rollout 也让瓶颈训练不足。ReFocus 将任务分解为子任务 DAG，用基于 DAG 的进度奖励训练并诊断瓶颈，再选择自适应练习窗口，在全局与局部 RL 间交替，对瓶颈片段分配额外交互。在 LIBERO-Long 和 RoboCasa365 上分别达到 97.8% 与 51.3% 成功率，真实 BreadBaker 任务达 95%。该框架提升了长程操作 RL 的瓶颈针对性与样本效率。
papers.abstract_en: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables vision-language-action policies to improve through environmental interaction. However, in long-horizon manipulation, sparse success/failure feedback provides little information about where policies encounter bottlenecks. Moreover, repeated full-task rollouts also leave these bottlenecks weakly analyzed and insufficiently practiced. To this end, we introduce ReFocus, a progress-guided multi-round RL framework that alternates between Global and Local RL to identify task-specific bottlenecks and allocate additional practice to them. Specifically, during Global RL, we decompose each task into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of subtasks. Then a DAG-based Progress Reward is leveraged for both policy training and bottleneck diagnosis. Based on the identified bottlenecks, ReFocus selects Adaptive Practice Windows, defining task segments from an entry stage to a target stage. It allocates additional interaction to these segments during Local RL while updating the entire policy. After that, it evaluates the policy to perform the full task for the next round of RL, forming an iteration between Global and Local RL. Experiments on LIBERO-Long and RoboCasa365 show that ReFocus achieves success rates of 97.8% and 51.3%, respectively, compared with 90.6% and 39.3% for the $π_{0.5}$ baseline. Furthermore, we evaluate a real-world adaptation on three long-horizon tasks. On BreadBaker, ReFocus achieves 95% success, compared with 30% for the $π_{0.5}$. Project page: https://refocus-robotics.github.io.

papers.title_en: PhysPPF: Learning Robotic Manipulation with Past, Present, and Future Physical Representations
papers.authors: Junjie Li, Dawei Yan, Guoting Wei, Ruike Song, Lu Wang, Qingguo Chen, Zhenbo Luo, Haokui Zhang, Chunhua Shen
papers.evidence: 统一时空物理令牌建模的视觉-语言-动作框架
papers.tldr: 现有VLA在需精确3D接触和长程协调的任务上仍受限，空间增强与时间建模多割裂且开销较高。PhysPPF在紧凑物理token空间统一时空建模：WWH蒸馏训练期感知教师，PPF维护有界过去记忆并联合推断现在与未来物理token。在SimplerEnv、CALVIN、LIBERO上分别较StarVLA基线提升17.2、29.3、3.5分，且延迟和参数开销适中。该工作为机器人操作提供低开销的时空物理表征方案。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have advanced robotic manipulation, yet complex tasks requiring both precise 3D contact and long-horizon coordination remain challenging. Most existing studies enhance spatial perception or temporal reasoning in VLAs separately. Spatial methods primarily inject geometric or affordance priors into current-frame perception without tracking multi-step transitions, while history-aware and world-model VLAs typically capture past context or future dynamics in 2D feature or pixel spaces, either lacking explicit 3D contact cues or incurring high generation overhead. To address this, we propose PhysPPF, a VLA framework that performs unified spatiotemporal modeling in a compact physical token space. Spatially, WWH (What-Where-How) distills pretrained perception teachers exclusively during training into compact token groups capturing what 3D structures occupy the scene, where to interact, and how the gripper should approach, without test-time 3D encoders. Temporally, operating directly in this WWH space without pixel reconstruction, PPF (Past-Present-Future) consolidates executed states into a bounded past physical memory and jointly infers present and future physical tokens via an asymmetric world model. Parallel gated branches then inject these past, present, and future representations into a flow-matching action expert to guide manipulation without cross-temporal interference. Extensive experiments on SimplerEnv, CALVIN, and LIBERO show that PhysPPF consistently outperforms existing spatial, history-aware, and world-model VLAs with modest latency and parameter overhead, improving over the StarVLA baseline by +17.2 points on SimplerEnv, +29.3 points on CALVIN, and +3.5 points on LIBERO.

papers.title_en: AsyncMixVLA: Runtime Asynchronous Robot Policy Switching for Adaptation to Dynamic Environments
papers.authors: Tamoghno Das, Keyon Jazayeri, Yerin Cho, Nazmul Takbir, Arshia Aravinthan, Nikil Dutt
papers.evidence: 跨视觉-语言-动作机器人策略的异步自适应切换
papers.tldr: VLA模型在物体中途移动等扰动下易失效，不同策略失败模式互补，但切换会因推理停顿或异步使用过期观测。AsyncMixVLA提出主动异步切换框架，用学习触发器权衡恢复收益与干预损害，并将高算力策略推理与已提交动作重叠、对齐预期接管状态。在LIBERO-Long扰动任务上，成功率由69.5%升至77.1%，总体84.9%接近同步切换的84.5%，中位交接延迟由226.5 ms降至0.1 ms；三类未见扰动达75.1%。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate visual observations and language instructions into robot actions, enabling general-purpose robotic control. However, environmental perturbations, such as objects moving during execution, can undermine their reliability. Different policies exhibit complementary failures under mid-rollout perturbations, motivating selective switching between policies for recovery. Such switching can stall the robot during inference of the newly invoked policy or, if performed asynchronously, act on stale observations. We present AsyncMixVLA, an adaptive inference framework for proactive, asynchronous switching across heterogeneous VLA policies. A learned trigger balances recovery potential against intervention harm to selectively escalate to a higher-compute policy. AsyncMixVLA overlaps its inference with committed outgoing actions and aligns its context to the anticipated takeover state. On LIBERO-Long with mid-rollout perturbations, AsyncMixVLA improves perturbed task success from 69.5% to 77.1% over the lightweight policy. It achieves 84.9% overall success, comparable to 84.5% for synchronous switching, while reducing median exposed handoff latency from 226.5 ms to 0.1 ms. Without retraining or recalibration, it achieves 75.1% success across three unseen perturbation families, compared with 71.3% for the stronger constituent policy in aggregate.

papers.title_en: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts
papers.authors: Chendong Xiang, Chengwen Zhang, Ruowen Zhao, Zeyuan Wang, Shuhe Huang, Rongxu Cui, Min Zhao, Fan Bao, Hengkai Tan, Jun Zhu
papers.evidence: 将人类视频与机器人观测映射为动作的上下文世界动作模型
papers.tldr: 人类视频上下文学习可让机器人无需参数更新完成新任务，但世界动作模型面临人机时序不对齐与动作捷径问题。Entangle用视频到视频生成构造对齐人机上下文，并以变长视频窗口和任务内对比目标训练。在Astribot S1六个未见任务均分83.5，RoboTwin七个未见任务成功率69.5%，超Zero-WAM 22.6个百分点。它还能在Context-OOD下迁移布局与工具变化指定的行为。
papers.abstract_en: In-context learning (ICL) enables foundation models to perform unseen tasks from context without parameter updates. In robotic manipulation, a human video provides the context that specifies how a task should be performed. However, scaling human-video ICL on world-action models (WAMs) faces two challenges: task-level human-robot pairs are not temporally aligned with robot actions, and standard action losses allow policies to rely on initial-scene or task-identity shortcuts rather than tracking the context. We present Entangle, an in-context world-action model that maps a single human video and current robot observations to future visual states and executable actions. To scale temporally aligned training data, we convert recorded robot videos into matched human contexts via video-to-video generation, supplemented by real paired recordings. For model training, we combine variable-length video windows with an intra-task contrastive objective that distinguishes the paired action trajectory from other executions of the same task, preventing task-identity shortcuts. Without task-specific fine-tuning, Entangle improves steadily as aligned training data scales, reaching an average score of 83.5/100 across six unseen tasks on an Astribot S1 robot, and achieves a 69.5% average success rate on seven unseen RoboTwin tasks, outperforming Zero-WAM by 22.6 percentage points. Under Context-OOD, although trained only on scene-aligned pairs, Entangle transfers context-specified behaviors across rearranged layouts and substituted tools.

papers.title_en: Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Qihang Chen, Tengjie Li, Hongwei Lu, Jason Wu, Chyna Qu, Shikui Tu, Lei Xu
papers.evidence: 视觉-语言-动作模型的空间锚定潜在前瞻
papers.tldr: VLA模型语义强，但精细操作仍需准确的空间定位与对未来场景演化的预判。SG-LL以当前空间状态为参照，先用冻结空间教师蒸馏几何先验，再由当前条件瓶颈预测可行动的近未来潜表示，并通过零初始化残差融合引导动作生成。在LIBERO-Plus、CALVIN和三项真实任务上，方法在仿真与真机均优于基线，说明空间锚定的潜前瞻能有效提升操作性能。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models benefit from strong semantic representations that support object recognition and instruction understanding. However, precise manipulation also depends on resolving object locations and workspace relations, and on selecting actions with an estimate of how the scene will evolve. Existing geometry-aware methods make the current scene more explicit, while predictive methods model future observations or representations. Yet future information is often neither grounded in a control-relevant spatial state nor directly used to guide action generation. We introduce Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead (SG-LL), which uses the grounded present as the reference for predicting an actionable near-future representation. A frozen spatial teacher first distills geometric priors into policy-connected spatial tokens. A current-conditioned bottleneck then learns a compact latent that captures future information relative to the present scene. This latent is predicted from the current policy context and initial Action Expert features, without access to future observations or the spatial teacher. Finally, zero-initialized residual fusion incorporates the predicted latent into the Action Expert to refine action generation. Experiments on LIBERO-Plus, CALVIN, and three real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate improvements over   in both simulation and real-robot settings.

papers.title_en: Embodied Neuro-symbolic AI: Making Robot Behavior Auditable, Safe, and Scalable
papers.authors: Ruwan Wickramarachchi, Jonathan Francis, Alessandro Oltramari
papers.evidence: 面向可审计安全VLA机器人行为的神经符号框架
papers.tldr: 当前VLA端到端机器人在分布偏移下泛化脆弱、物理与因果推理不足、细粒度控制不稳定，且难以表达和审计安全禁令。作者提出具身神经符号AI，将学习式感知、规划与控制同机器可读背景知识和形式化约束结合。通过知识引导感知、约束感知符号规划与混合学习，使机器人可推理环境、适应新任务并机器校验安全合规。该范式面向可扩展、可信的实际部署，但摘要未给出量化实验。
papers.abstract_en: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) end-to-end systems have driven major progress in robot learning, yet they still face persistent barriers to dependable real-world deployment. In practice, these models often exhibit brittle generalization under distribution shift (i.e., novel objects, layouts, lighting, or contact conditions), limited physical and causal reasoning, and inconsistent fine-grained motor control. Critically, many VLA pipelines offer limited ways to express and audit what a robot must not do, making it difficult to provide assurance in safety-critical settings. These limitations constrain scalability, maintainability, and trust when robots move beyond controlled demonstrations. We propose Embodied Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) AI: a deployment-oriented paradigm that integrates learned perception, planning and control with explicit, machine-readable background knowledge and formal constraints. By combining knowledge-guided perception, constraint-aware symbolic planning, and hybrid learning, Embodied NeSy AI enables robots to reason about their environment, adapt to new tasks, and provide auditable, machine-checkable compliance with safety and operational requirements, thus supporting scalable, trustworthy robot deployment.

papers.title_en: One Phase Is Enough: Sim-to-Real Transfer with Direct Visual Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: John Marangola, Antonia Bronars, Younghyo Park, Stephen Andrews, Kushal Kedia, Pulkit Agrawal
papers.evidence: 面向仿真到现实机器人操作策略的直接视觉强化学习
papers.tldr: 视觉强化学习从仿真迁移到真实机器人仍受限于表示学习效率低，常见两阶段教师蒸馏学生会显著掉点。DRIFT采用冻结的预训练基础视觉编码器，让强化学习只学习控制，从而直接进行一阶段视觉RL并利用快速光栅化仿真渲染迁移。在匹配架构、观测和算力下，其平均真实成功率较两阶段蒸馏相对提升58.8%，分布外仿真优势从约9%扩大到超61%。这表明冻结视觉表征可提升泛化并简化仿真到真实迁移流程。
papers.abstract_en: Sim-to-real reinforcement learning (RL) has enabled impressive robotic behaviors, yet deploying policies directly from vision remains challenging. A common approach first trains a teacher policy with RL using privileged state observations, then distills its behavior into a vision-based student via imitation. However, the resulting student can substantially underperform its teacher. Directly training visual policies with RL offers a promising alternative, but learning task-relevant visual representations from scratch can be sample-inefficient, making one-phase visual RL intractable. We propose DRIFT, a simple recipe for efficient one-phase visual RL using image observations available at test time. Our key insight is to use frozen, pretrained foundation vision encoders, allowing RL to focus on learning control from existing visual representations. Freezing the encoder avoids costly backpropagation through the vision backbone, while its pretrained representations enable real-world transfer from fast, rasterized simulation rendering. Under matched architectures, observations, and compute budgets, DRIFT outperforms two-phase distillation and achieves a 58.8% relative improvement in average real-world success rate across three manipulation tasks. Controlled simulation evaluations demonstrate that DRIFT's relative advantage grows from roughly 9% in-distribution to over 61% under out-of-distribution shifts, suggesting that stronger generalization contributes to superior real-world transfer. Project website: https://jmarangola.github.io/one-phase-visual-rl/

papers.title_en: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming for Robot Foundation Models
papers.authors: Kyle Coelho, Eugen Solowjow
papers.evidence: 无需额外数据与训练即可编辑预训练视觉-语言-动作策略的权重
papers.tldr: 机器人基础模型常因重复卡住状态而失败，且难以额外采数或训练。本文用权重空间编程让语言模型代理直接改写预训练VLA策略的极少量参数。方法在动作专家近静默神经元写入指定纠正行为，使编辑仅在失败情境触发。仿真中pi0.5仅改约0.0002%参数便提升反复失败成功率，已微调策略亦有效，为无需数据训练的故障修复提供轻量路径。
papers.abstract_en: This paper demonstrates an approach for correcting failures of robot foundation models (RFMs) without additional data collection, demonstrations, or training. We apply weight-space programming (WSP), in which a language-model agent directly reads and writes a neural network's parameters, to a large, pre-trained vision-language-action policy. The idea is simple: many policy failures are not random but repeatedly land in the same recognizable stuck state, so if that state is visible in the model's internal activations, a small edit could trigger a corrective movement while leaving the rest of the model's parameters unchanged. A core design choice is where to write the edit: repurposing a few near-silent neurons in the action expert lets the edit switch on in situations associated with the failure and produce a corrective movement, such as lowering the gripper toward the target, that is specified directly rather than learned through training. Empirically, when applied to the pi0.5 policy in simulation, we find that edits to roughly 0.0002% of the parameters can improve success on recurring failures, including for a policy that was already fine-tuned on its task. Reversed and random edits indicate that the gains come from the intended behavior, and the approach works best when the failure situation is recognizable and a simple correction can address it.

papers.title_en: ActiveBridge: Scaling Active Prior for Robots through Egocentric Perception-Interaction Modeling
papers.authors: Zixiao Gu, Qiren Qin, Yu He, Zhengyang Liu, Da Huang, Hongquan Zhang, Simo Wu, Peng Zhou, Guangnan Ye, Yunbo Wang, Yanwei Fu
papers.evidence: 通过世界-动作建模学习可主动控制视角的视觉运动操作策略
papers.tldr: 现有机器人基础模型多被动利用给定观察，忽略自我中心视频中人类主动寻求信息的先验，在非结构化场景受限。ActiveBridge 通过世界-动作建模学习该主动先验，并用指令条件模型联合预测未来视频与头腕动作轨迹。机器人仅凭单头相机以头部动作主动调整视角，无需腕部相机。实验在主动操作任务上优于基线，消融验证联合头腕监督有效，为机器人主动感知迁移提供新路径。
papers.abstract_en: Robotics foundation models are now widely used for manipulation, and egocentric videos offer rich data for scaling. However, existing methods overlook the human active priors captured in egocentric videos, which limits performance in unstructured scenes. They act on given observations instead of actively seeking information as humans do. We propose ActiveBridge, a training framework that learns these human active priors and transfers them to robots through world-action modeling. We design a robot that actively controls its viewpoint through head actions to acquire the visual information needed for manipulation using a single head camera, without wrist cameras. During human training, an instruction-conditioned model jointly predicts future egocentric videos and synchronized head-wrist action trajectories, with head actions providing explicit supervision for active perception. Experiments show that ActiveBridge outperforms baselines on active manipulation tasks, while ablations demonstrate the benefit of joint head-wrist action supervision.

papers.title_en: FN-Prune: Training-Free Expert Pruning with Finite RMSNorm Perturbations
papers.authors: Zeyan Li, Jianfeng Xu
papers.evidence: 基于校准token的免训练专家剪枝以降低大型MoE语言模型内存占用
papers.tldr: 混合专家语言模型可通过专家剪枝降低显存占用，但保留模型质量取决于删除哪些专家。现有频率和幅值评分孤立衡量专家，忽略归一化会同时改变残差方向与剩余贡献尺度。FN-Prune提出免训练准则：固定原始路由与权重，比较减去各专家贡献前后RMSNorm输出的平方差，并在校准token上单次平均打分。按层均匀比例物理删除低分专家，推理时在幸存者中重路由。50%删除率下，其在Qwen3、ERNIE、OLMoE上的WikiText-2困惑度优于已发表最佳方法，OLMoE降低32%，GSM8K准确率在Qwen3和ERNIE上分别提升7.5和7.0个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: Expert pruning reduces the memory footprint of mixture-of-experts language models, but retaining model quality depends on which experts are removed. Frequency- and magnitude-based scores measure the expert in isolation and overlook how normalization consumes its contribution: subtracting one expert changes both the direction of the residual stream and the scale applied to what remains. We propose FN-Prune, a training-free criterion that compares the next RMSNorm outputs before and after subtracting each router-weighted expert contribution, holding original routes and weights fixed. Squared differences are averaged over all calibration tokens in one pass; low-scoring experts are physically deleted at uniform per-layer ratios, and inference reroutes among survivors. At 50% expert removal, FN-Prune achieves lower WikiText-2 perplexity than the best published methods on Qwen3, ERNIE, and OLMoE, including a 32% reduction on OLMoE. At the same budget, GSM8K accuracy improves over the best published methods by 7.5 and 7.0 percentage points on Qwen3 and ERNIE, respectively, while multiple-choice gains remain task-dependent.

papers.title_en: Two-Stage Post-Training for Flow-Based Embodied Foundation Models
papers.authors: Jiaming Zhang, Yao Lyu, Haoning Wang, Yongjun Chen, Liping Zhang, Shengbo Eben Li
papers.evidence: 面向可靠任务执行的流式具身基础模型两阶段后训练
papers.tldr: 大规模预训练虽提供通用能力，但具身模型可靠执行仍需后训练；多任务SFT有分布不匹配，RL受稀疏奖励和任务进度不均限制。本文提出流式具身基础模型的两阶段后训练框架，从条件流匹配速度回归构造蒸馏目标：先用MOPD整合专家，再结合RL与按采样噪声加权、仅用于失败轨迹的教师蒸馏。多模型多基准实验显示其优于联合SFT、超过教师聚合成功率，且比直接RL更省环境交互。
papers.abstract_en: Large-scale pretraining provides embodied models with general capabilities, but reliable task execution still requires post training. In multitask settings, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) faces distribution mismatch between training and deployment, whereas reinforcement learning (RL) is limited by sparse rewards and uneven learning progress across tasks. Multi-teacher on policy distillation (MOPD) consolidates expert capabilities through dense supervision on the model's own trajectories, but achieving performance beyond the teachers remains challenging. We propose a two-stage post training framework for flow-based embodied models, constructing distillation objectives from the velocity regression formulation of conditional flow matching. Stage 1 efficiently consolidates expert capabilities through MOPD. Stage 2 combines RL with teacher distillation that weights velocity errors according to the sampling noise, where distillation is restricted to failed trajectories to supplement sparse rewards with dense guidance without directly constraining successful behaviors. Experiments across multiple models and benchmarks show that the framework outperforms joint SFT and exceeds the corresponding teachers' aggregate success rates. Sample efficiency comparisons show higher success rates than direct RL with fewer environment interactions.

papers.title_en: Sparse Poison, Strong Hijack: Efficient Trajectory-Level Backdoors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Only 1\% Poisoning
papers.authors: Simin Huang, Jiawei Chen, Shaolong Zhu, Qiwei Liang, Zhaoxia Yin
papers.evidence: 视觉-语言-动作机器人操作模型中的轨迹级后门威胁
papers.tldr: 视觉-语言-动作模型依赖示范数据，易受轨迹级后门攻击，但低毒化率下目标轨迹监督稀缺。本文提出视觉、语言与动作引导的两阶段协同优化框架：先优化3D触发器的纹理、平移与尺度，再用源选择双LoRA解耦干净与后门更新并融合策略。仅1%毒化数据时，OpenVLA-OFT在LIBERO-Spatial上达到86.4%目标成功率和95.2%干净任务成功率，真机亦实现轨迹级劫持。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models advance robotic manipulation, but their reliance on demonstrations exposes them to backdoor threats. Among these threats, trajectory-level targeted backdoors are particularly challenging and may pose greater safety risks than behavior-disrupting attacks: rather than merely causing task failures or local action deviations, they must sustain closed-loop redirection to complete an attacker-specified multi-step task. To reliably induce such behaviors, existing methods typically rely on high poisoning rates to obtain sufficient target-trajectory supervision. However, high poisoning rates may compromise clean-task performance, whereas low rates leave target-trajectory supervision scarce and backdoor learning vulnerable to interference from dominant clean-task updates. To resolve this trade-off at low poisoning rates, we propose a two-stage co-optimization framework guided by vision, language, and action. Stage I freezes the policy and uses differentiable rendering and multimodal supervision to optimize a 3D trigger's texture, translation, and scale, strengthening trigger-target associations from limited poisoned demonstrations. Building on the optimized trigger, Stage II applies source-selective dual-LoRA adaptation to decouple clean and backdoor updates and mitigate their interference, followed by learned column-wise calibration and analytic fusion into a unified policy. Experiments on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, $π_0$, and $π_{0.5}$ across four LIBERO suites show consistent gains over all evaluated attack baselines. With only 1% poisoned data, our method achieves 86.4% target success and 95.2% clean-task success on OpenVLA-OFT in LIBERO-Spatial. Real-robot trials also demonstrate trajectory-level hijacking.

papers.title_en: RoboRecast: Intent-Preserving Demonstration Augmentation via Diagnosis-Driven Optimization
papers.authors: Yushi Long, Juzhan Xu, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Yin Chen, Sida Peng, Ruizhen Hu, Xiaowei Zhou
papers.evidence: 面向机器人操作策略学习的仿真示范增强
papers.tldr: 真实机器人操作演示采集成本高，仿真增强常因物体、布局或本体变化导致源动作语义不合理或物理不可行。RoboRecast以智能体优化框架保留源任务所需交互，联合优化仿真场景与机器人运动，并利用仿真反馈诊断失败、修正场景或运动参数并复测。在目标演示可用时，加入其合成数据可提升真实单臂与仿真双臂任务策略成功率；无目标演示时也能适配新物体或新本体。该工作为跨场景、跨本体的演示增强提供了可诊断、可执行的方案。
papers.abstract_en: Collecting diverse real-world manipulation demonstrations is costly, motivating the use of simulation to augment existing demonstrations for robot policy learning. When objects, layouts, or robots change, transferring motions from a source demonstration can produce behavior that is semantically implausible or physically infeasible in the new setting. We introduce RoboRecast, an agentic optimization framework that preserves the interactions required by the source task while jointly optimizing the simulated scene and robot motion to make those interactions executable in the target setting. When an interaction fails, the agent uses simulation feedback to diagnose the cause, revise the relevant scene or motion parameters, and test whether the revision resolves the failure. This flexibility allows RoboRecast to generate synthetic data from both human and robot demonstrations and to adapt them to new layouts, objects, and robot embodiments. When target demonstrations are available, adding RoboRecast data improves policy success on both real-world single-arm and simulated bimanual tasks. Even without demonstrations in the target configuration, RoboRecast adapts source demonstrations to support policy learning with new objects or robot embodiments.
